title: Dreyer et al. 2023 — A large EEG database with users' profile information for motor imagery brain-computer interface research
description: A large EEG database from 87 healthy participants recorded during a single-day motor imagery brain-computer interface (BCI) experiment. The data are organized into three datasets (A, B, C) that share the same Graz protocol of left- and right-hand motor imagery, with 240 trials per participant (over 20,800 trials in total). It also includes demographic, personality and cognitive-trait information, which supports research on links between user profiles and BCI performance, cross-user machine learning, and user-profile-informed classification.
methods_description: Participants performed a Graz protocol motor imagery BCI task with 6 runs: 2 calibration runs with sham feedback and 4 online training runs with real feedback. Each run had 40 trials of 8 s. EEG was recorded with g.USBAmp active electrodes at 512 Hz, using OpenViBE. Online processing used participant-specific most-discriminant frequency band selection (5-35 Hz), a Butterworth filter, CSP and an LDA classifier. Participants also completed questionnaires on demographics, personality (16PF5), cognitive traits, spatial abilities and learning style.
